brief.greeting: Good morning. The Slovak web crawl just exposed a half‑percent farm of AI‑spun pages.

stories.headline: LLM Agent Finds 1.4M Fake Docs in Slovak Crawl
stories.body: **Agent on the hunt:** An LLM‑driven auditor scanned 26.5 M Slovak documents, flagging 1,408,437 machine‑generated pages (5.32% of the set). The run cost about $2.50 and finished in under a second.
stories.why: Spotting synthetic content helps you trust data pipelines and avoid polluted training sets.

stories.headline: VERA Dashboard Scores LLMs Against EU AI Act
stories.body: **Compliance made visual:** VERA, an open‑source dashboard, logs energy use per benchmark and checks twelve EU AI‑Act technical criteria, now running at a major European bank.
stories.why: You can measure regulatory risk and power draw before you ship a model to production.

stories.headline: DeepMind Publishes 10‑Meter Global Forest Type Map
stories.body: **Pixels of trees:** The new map classifies every 10‑meter patch on Earth into distinct forest types, giving researchers a uniform view of global canopy diversity.
stories.why: Fine‑grained land data can improve climate models you might train on satellite imagery.

quick_hits.text: **Security:** .NET 10.0 and Debian bind9 patched across major distros.
**API:** OpenAI’s Decisions API offers cheap, sub‑second calls for app logic.
**iOS on Android:** Hackios runs full iOS 16.5 firmware in a browser.
**Language:** L4 introduces reversible, linearly‑typed IR for compiler research.
**Fuzzing:** New kernel fuzzer separates input generation from thread scheduling.
**Guest investigators:** Anthropic seeks life‑science proposals from external teams.

brief.sign_off: That’s the night, see you tomorrow

highlights.title: Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
highlights.summary: An LLM‑driven agent audited the 26.5 M‑document Slovak portion of FineWeb2, uncovering a machine‑generated content farm of 1,408,437 documents (5.32% of the corpus).
highlights.detail: The agent operated via a read‑only, budgeted API and compiled findings into executable tests validated by native speakers. Three runs each identified seven issues across four phenomena. The full‑corpus scan required no GPU and ran in under a second, demonstrating a cheap, scalable debugging approach.

highlights.title: Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination
highlights.summary: Four open‑source LLMs (8‑27 B parameters) were evaluated on the Spanish MIR residency exam (1,552 questions), with the three larger models ranking roughly between 600 and 3,000 candidates and leaving 41‑43 specialties open.
highlights.detail: The study examined model uncertainty, clinical reasoning, and image usage, finding that abstention never improved outcomes because even the least confident answers exceeded the 25% break‑even threshold. Results suggest open models can be competitive but still lack reliable self‑assessment.

highlights.title: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
highlights.summary: Anthropic announced a program to donate agent skills to the Agentic AI Foundation.
highlights.detail: The initiative aims to share capabilities developed by Anthropic's agents with the broader community, fostering collaborative advancement of agentic AI. No further technical details were provided in the announcement.

highlights.title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
highlights.summary: VERA is an open‑source self‑hosted dashboard that scores LLMs against twelve EU AI Act technical requirements and records energy consumption per benchmark run, deployed at a large European bank.
highlights.detail: The tool builds on the COMPL‑AI interpretation of the EU AI Act, organizing evidence into six principle groups and eighteen technical requirements, of which twelve are currently benchmarkable. VERA simplifies the workflow for non‑engineer reviewers by providing a UI for model selection and benchmark execution.

highlights.title: The Reversible Intermediate Language L4, its Type System, and its Bidirectional Small-Step Semantics
highlights.summary: The paper defines L4, a reversible, linearly‑typed intermediate language with a bidirectional small‑step semantics for compiling reversible programs.
highlights.detail: L4 generalises the earlier RSSA form and draws inspiration from HSSA, offering direction indicators that allow forward and backward execution to switch dynamically. This facilitates compilation to reversible hardware.

items.title: Beyond tree cover: mapping the world’s forest types
items.summary: DeepMind released a global map that classifies every 10‑meter patch of land into distinct forest types.
items.detail: The dataset provides a fine‑grained view of forest distribution worldwide, enabling ecological research and policy planning. It represents a step beyond traditional tree‑cover maps by distinguishing among multiple forest categories.

items.title: Build more responsive apps with the Decisions API
items.summary: OpenAI introduced the Decisions API, offering fast, low‑cost decision‑making calls for application developers.
items.detail: The API is designed to deliver focused predictions with minimal latency and expense, targeting use‑cases that require frequent, lightweight decisions rather than full‑scale language generation.

items.title: Open call for guest investigators in the life sciences
items.summary: Anthropic is inviting guest investigators to propose life‑science research projects.
items.detail: The open call targets external researchers to explore applications of foundation models in biology and medicine, offering access to Anthropic's resources and potential collaboration opportunities.

items.title: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK partner to advance AI safety and security
items.summary: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK have formed a partnership to work on AI safety, security, and technical research.
items.detail: The collaboration aims to develop safeguards and strengthen the digital ecosystem, leveraging NASK’s expertise in cybersecurity and OpenAI’s AI capabilities.

items.title: What FDE means at OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI outlines its forward‑deployed engineering (FDE) model for rapid, on‑site AI system development.
items.detail: FDE teams embed engineers directly with product groups to iterate quickly, focusing on safety, reliability, and performance in production environments.

items.title: Ensemble forecasting with IBM Granite time-series models
items.summary: IBM released Granite time‑series models for ensemble forecasting tasks.
items.detail: The models are hosted on Hugging Face, support probabilistic forecasts, and are intended for applications like weather prediction and demand planning.

items.title: Security updates for Thursday
items.summary: Multiple Linux distributions issued security updates covering dozens of packages on Thursday.
items.detail: Updates address vulnerabilities in runtimes, web servers, and system libraries across AlmaLinux, Arch, Debian, Fedora, Gentoo, Mageia, Oracle, and Red Hat, requiring administrators to apply the patches promptly.

items.title: Run full iOS 16.5 firmware on Android Devices
items.summary: Hackios provides a web tool that runs full iOS 16.5 firmware on Android devices.
items.detail: The service emulates the iOS environment, allowing developers and hobbyists to test iOS apps without Apple hardware, though performance and compatibility are limited by Android hardware constraints.

items.title: [$] Rust features in the future
items.summary: At Kangrejos 2026, Josh Triplett outlined upcoming Rust kernel features such as type system refinements, syntax tweaks, and a smarter borrow checker.
items.detail: The talk highlighted how these enhancements could simplify kernel code and enable new patterns, but they remain work‑in‑progress within the Rust project. Developers are encouraged to track the Rust roadmap for implementation timelines.

items.title: [$] The end of __get_user() and __put_user()
items.summary: A 48‑part patch series by Linus Torvalds removes __get_user() and __put_user() primitives from the Linux 7.4 kernel.
items.detail: The cleanup eliminates long‑standing user‑space memory access helpers that have been superseded, reducing kernel surface area. The change required careful coordination due to the extensive codebase that still referenced these functions.

items.title: KeePassXC 2.8.0 released
items.summary: KeePassXC 2.8.0 adds Qt6 migration, Wayland auto‑type, and ships native ARM64 builds for Windows and an experimental AArch64 AppImage for Linux.
items.detail: The release also introduces configurable shortcuts, remote sync support, and quick unlock options on macOS and Linux via Polkit. These updates address long‑awaited feature requests and improve cross‑platform performance.

items.title: An Open Source Linear Capacitive Encoder
items.summary: Hackaday details an open‑source linear capacitive encoder design derived from digital caliper technology.
items.detail: The project provides schematics and firmware for a low‑cost, high‑resolution position sensor that can be fabricated with standard PCB processes. It targets hobbyists and embedded developers needing precise linear measurement.

items.title: The Reversible Intermediate Language L4, its Type System, and its Bidirectional Small-Step Semantics
items.summary: The paper defines L4, a reversible, linearly‑typed intermediate language with a bidirectional small‑step semantics for compiling reversible programs.
items.detail: L4 generalises the earlier RSSA form and draws inspiration from HSSA, offering direction indicators that allow forward and backward execution to switch dynamically. This facilitates compilation to reversible hardware.

items.title: Breaking the Coupling: Efficient Concurrency Fuzzing for Linux Kernel Data Race Detection
items.summary: A new concurrency fuzzing approach separates input generation from thread‑interleaving exploration, using May Race Pairs to focus scheduling on promising inputs.
items.detail: By decoupling these phases, the framework reduces wasted scheduling effort on low‑yield inputs and improves detection of real data races in the Linux kernel. MRPs are collected during unscheduled runs and guide targeted mutations.

items.title: Automated Enrichment Analysis with GraphRAG: Efficient Multi-Database ORA Extraction and Biological Interpretation
items.summary: Graph-Based Over-Representation Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GBOR-RAG) unifies multiple gene-set databases into a term‑gene graph and extracts a compact evidence subgraph to condition an LLM for biologically faithful enrichment interpretations.
items.detail: The framework first scores over‑representation on the unified graph, then retrieves a connected subgraph that preserves cross‑database links and gene‑level support. A claim‑level faithfulness metric evaluates whether generated statements are directly backed by the retrieved evidence.

items.title: Evolving Federated Density Peak Clustering with Shuffler-Based Anonymization
items.summary: Evolving Federated Density Peak Clustering (eFDPC) combines fuzzy data‑stream clustering with density‑peak methods to enable a one‑shot federated clustering that limits client‑server exchanges and preserves unlinkability.
items.detail: Each client builds micro‑clusters locally and shares only anonymized summaries via a shuffler, preventing attribution of data to any single participant. The approach aligns with single‑pass streaming algorithms, making it suitable for privacy‑sensitive distributed environments.

items.title: TT-SAX: A Two-Track Time Series Symbolization for Natural Language Shape Querying
items.summary: TT‑SAX redesigns Symbolic Aggregate approXimation to include directional information at appropriate scales, addressing three limitations of prior symbolizations for natural‑language shape queries on time‑series databases.
items.detail: The new two‑track design adds explicit direction symbols, aggregates direction over longer intervals, and replaces arbitrary letters with meaningful tokens, improving interpretability for plain‑language queries that ask how a series moves.

items.title: Almost tight distributed approximation for domination in sparse graph classes
items.summary: A deterministic constant‑round LOCAL algorithm achieves a (d+1+ε) approximation for Minimum Dominating Set on bounded‑average‑degree graphs, yielding (7+ε)‑approximation for planar graphs and (5+ε)‑approximation for bounded‑Euler‑genus graphs.
items.detail: The result extends near‑optimal guarantees from minor‑free to broader bounded‑expansion classes, improving on prior work limited to proper minor‑closed families. The algorithm runs in constant rounds regardless of graph size, making it practical for distributed settings.

items.title: Meloong-Git/PCL
items.summary: Meloong‑Git/PCL is a Chinese‑language Minecraft launcher named Plain Craft Launcher.
items.detail: The repository provides the source code and binaries for launching the Minecraft game with a custom user interface, targeting users who prefer a lightweight, locally‑run launcher.

items.title: NanmiCoder/MediaCrawler
items.summary: NanmiCoder/MediaCrawler is a Python tool that scrapes comments and posts from platforms such as Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Bilibili, Weibo, Baidu Tieba, Zhihu, and others.
items.detail: The crawler supports multiple media sites, extracting both content and associated comment threads, enabling large‑scale data collection for analysis or archiving. It is open‑source and configurable for different target platforms.

items.title: apache/iggy
items.summary: Apache Iggy is a Rust‑based message streaming platform marketed as hyper‑efficient and low‑latency.
items.detail: Iggy aims to provide faster data pipelines than traditional brokers by leveraging Rust's performance and zero‑copy techniques. It targets use cases like real‑time analytics and event sourcing. The project is open source and part of the Apache incubator.

items.title: deepseek-ai/3FS
items.summary: deepseek-ai/3FS is a C++ distributed file system built for AI training and inference workloads.
items.detail: 3FS focuses on high throughput and low latency to handle large model checkpoints and dataset shards. It integrates with common AI frameworks and supports scaling across multiple nodes. The system is open source and positioned as an alternative to existing cloud storage solutions for AI pipelines.

items.title: electron/electron
items.summary: electron/electron enables developers to create cross‑platform desktop applications using web technologies.
items.detail: Electron bundles Chromium and Node.js, allowing a single codebase to run on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It powers many popular apps such as VS Code and Slack. The project continues active development with frequent releases.

items.title: google-pytorch/torch_tpu
items.summary: google-pytorch/torch_tpu provides PyTorch support for TPU hardware.
items.detail: The repository adds backend kernels and integration layers so PyTorch models can run on Google's Tensor Processing Units. It aims to bring the familiar PyTorch workflow to TPU‑accelerated training and inference, complementing existing XLA support.
